# Upstox FY21 net loss doubles as employee charges, other expenses weigh

By [Nikhil Patwardhan](/author/nikhil-patwardhan)

* 16 Feb 2022

* **Listen to Story**

![Upstox FY21 net loss doubles as employee charges, other expenses weigh](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.vccircle.com%2Fuploads%2F2020%2F04%2Flossrfxl.jpg&w=3840&q=75)

Credit: 123RF.com

Online stock-broking company Upstox’s net loss widened twofold for 2020-21 (FY21) as the company’s employee benefit costs and other expenses soared during the year, regulatory filings show.

[Upstox](tag/upstox), managed and operated by [RKSV Securities India Pvt Ltd](tag/rksv-securities-india-pvt-ltd), reported a net loss of ‚¹71.67 crore for FY21 against ‚¹37.98 crore a year earlier, the company’s filings with the ministry of corporate affairs show. While the company’s operating revenue surged over 200% to ‚¹385.64 crore for the year from ‚¹124.90 crore in 2019-20 (FY20), its operating expenses jumped nearly 170% to ‚¹497.32 crore, weighing on the company’s bottom line.

Upstox’s employee benefit expenses and other expenses, which include after-sale service expenses, advertising promotional expenses, legal and professional charges and commission paid to sole selling agents, among other heads, soared during the year, the filings show.

Advertisement

While employee benefit costs doubled to ‚¹65.10 crore, other expenses nearly tripled to ‚¹426 crore. The company reported numbers on a standalone basis. Upstox also has a subsidiary for commodities trading called [RKSV Commodities India Pvt Ltd](tag/rksv-commodities-india-pvt-ltd).

The surge in demand for online broking in the pandemic-battered year helped Upstox report a strong growth in its operating revenue. According to the data from the National Securities Depository and Central Depository Services, 14.2 million new demat accounts were opened in FY21, a near three-fold increase from FY20’s 4.9 million.

Upstox’s closest competitors [Groww](tag/groww), operated by NextBillion Technology Pvt Ltd, and [Zerodha](tag/zerodha) Broking Ltd, too, reported a sharp rise in their revenues for FY21. Zerodha, India’s largest broking firm, reported a profit of ‚¹1,122 crore, while Groww turned profitable for the first time with a ‚¹2.73 crore net profit.

Advertisement

Upstox [joined the unicorn](https://www.vccircle.com/upstox-raises-25-mn-from-tiger-global-affiliate-at-3-39-bn-valuation) club in November last year after it raised $25 million as a part of its Series C funding round led by Tiger Global Management. Unicorns are companies with over $1 billion in valuation. Prior to that, the company [had raised  $25 million](https://www.vccircle.com/tiger-global-invests-in-online-stock-brokerage-company-upstox) from Tiger Global Management’s affiliate Scott Shleifer in 2019. The company had also raised [$4 million in 2016](https://www.vccircle.com/online-stock-broker-rksv-raises-4m-series-funding-kalaari-others/) in a Series A funding round led by Kalaari Capital.

Upstox is a discount stockbroking platform, founded in 2009 by co-founders Ravi Kumar and Shrini Viswanath, and onboarded Kavitha Subramanian as its third co-founder in 2016.  The startup provides products and tools such as web-, desktop- and mobile-based trading platforms, and application programming interfaces (APIs) for developers. The company offers free delivery trades and charges for advanced methods such as intraday trades and futures and options.

results.title: Rebel Foods FY26 Results Show Higher Revenue and Lower Losses - Indian Retailer
results.content:
Advertising and promotional spending rose 26 percent to Rs 193.9 crore, while depreciation and amortisation expenses reached Rs 153.5 crore. Other operational costs, including outsourced delivery services, legal and professional fees, power, and fuel expenses, amounted to Rs 404.2 crore.

Overall expenditure increased 14 percent to Rs 2,265.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,986.6 crore a year earlier. However, revenue growth outpaced the rise in costs, helping the company reduce its net loss from Rs 336.6 crore in FY25 to Rs 281.8 crore in FY26. [...] India remained the company’s largest market, contributing 85.5 percent of operating revenue. Revenue from India grew 18 percent to Rs 1,667.7 crore, while international operations recorded a 39 percent increase, generating Rs 283.8 crore during FY26.

Rebel Foods also reported Rs 43.3 crore in non-operating income, including interest earnings and gains from financial assets, taking its total income to Rs 1,994.9 crore for the fiscal year.

On the expenditure front, the cost of materials remained the company’s biggest expense, rising 16 percent to Rs 784.4 crore and accounting for nearly 35 percent of total spending. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 412.3 crore, while brokerage and commission costs increased 31 percent to Rs 317.7 crore. [...] India continued to be the company’s largest market, contributing Rs 893.3 crore in revenue. Meanwhile, international operations recorded significant growth, with overseas revenue increasing fourfold to Rs 22.85 crore.

In addition to its core business income, Curefoods generated Rs 18.6 crore through non-operating sources such as interest income and gains from mutual fund investments. This pushed its total income for the fiscal year to Rs 934.8 crore.

Commission expenses climbed 22 percent to Rs 166.8 crore, while depreciation and amortisation charges rose 24 percent to Rs 100.6 crore. In contrast, advertising and promotional spending declined 10 percent to Rs 79 crore during the year.

Rebel Foods FY26 Results Show Higher Revenue and Lower Losses

![Rebel Foods FY26 Results Show Higher Revenue and Lower Losses](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-18T114718.036.jpg "Rebel Foods FY26 Results Show Higher Revenue and Lower Losses")

Cloud kitchen operator Rebel Foods posted improved financial results for FY26, driven by stronger revenue growth and a reduction in losses. **The company reported a 21 percent year-on-year increase in operating revenue, while its net loss narrowed by 16 percent to Rs 281.8 crore for the financial year ended March 2026.**

**Rebel Foods' revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,951.6 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 1,617.4 crore in FY25.**

**The company operates several food delivery brands including Faasos, Behrouz Biryani, The Good Bowl, LunchBox, Oven Story Pizza, and The Biryani Life.** Its primary source of income continues to be the sale of food products through its owned brands, while franchise and commission income contribute a smaller share.

**Revenue from the sale of goods increased 21 percent to Rs 1,891.8 crore, accounting for nearly 97 percent of total operating revenue.** Franchise income rose 10 percent to Rs 15.6 crore, whereas commission income declined 7 percent to Rs 17.1 crore. Other operating income, including delivery-related services, stood at Rs 27 crore during the year.

**India remained the company’s largest market, contributing 85.5 percent of operating revenue.** Revenue from India grew 18 percent to Rs 1,667.7 crore, while international operations recorded a 39 percent increase, generating Rs 283.8 crore during FY26.

**Rebel Foods also reported Rs 43.3 crore in non-operating income, including interest earnings and gains from financial assets, taking its total income to Rs 1,994.9 crore for the fiscal year.**

On the expenditure front, the cost of materials remained the company’s biggest expense, rising 16 percent to Rs 784.4 crore and accounting for nearly 35 percent of total spending. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 412.3 crore, while brokerage and commission costs increased 31 percent to Rs 317.7 crore.

**Advertising and promotional spending rose 26 percent to Rs 193.9 crore, while depreciation and amortisation expenses reached Rs 153.5 crore.** Other operational costs, including outsourced delivery services, legal and professional fees, power, and fuel expenses, amounted to Rs 404.2 crore.

**Overall expenditure increased 14 percent to Rs 2,265.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,986.6 crore a year earlier.** However, revenue growth outpaced the rise in costs, helping the company reduce its net loss from Rs 336.6 crore in FY25 to Rs 281.8 crore in FY26.

**The company also reported an improvement in profitability metrics, with its EBITDA loss narrowing to Rs 105.7 crore and the EBITDA margin improving to negative 5.4 percent.** At the unit level, Rebel Foods spent Rs 1.16 to generate every rupee of operating revenue, compared to Rs 1.23 in the previous fiscal year.

**Rebel Foods ended FY26 with a cash and bank balance of Rs 112 crore, nearly double the previous year, while its current assets stood at Rs 632 crore.**

Backed by investors including Peak XV Partners, Coatue, QIA, and Lightbox, the company has raised nearly $803 million in funding to date.

Rebel Foods Approves Fresh ESOP Grant as It Works Towards Profitability

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

![Rebel Foods Approves Fresh ESOP Grant as It Works Towards Profitability](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-27T121907.926.jpg)

Rebel Foods, the cloud kitchen operator behind brands such as Faasos, Behrouz Biryani and Oven Story Pizza, has approved a fresh employee stock option (ESOP) grant worth approximately Rs 170 crore for its five co-founders.

**The company's board has cleared the grant of 25.36 lakh ESOPs at an exercise price of Rs 670 per option, taking the total value of the allocation to around Rs 170 crore.**

**Co-founder and CEO Ankush Grover received the largest share, with 17.09 lakh options valued at Rs 114.51 crore.** Co-founder Jaydeep Barman was allocated 4.27 lakh options worth Rs 28.63 crore. **The remaining three co-founders, Piyush Kakkad, Jayeep Barman and Ankur Sharma, each received 1.34 lakh options valued at approximately Rs 8.95 crore.**

Grover took over from Jaydeep Barman in July 2025 and has since been responsible for leading the company's efforts to achieve profitability and prepare for a potential public listing. **A substantial portion of his ESOP allocation appears to be linked to the achievement of specific milestones.**

**The grant comes as Rebel Foods works to improve its financial performance while expanding its cloud kitchen business.** In FY26, the company recorded growth in operating revenue alongside a reduction in losses.

According to its FY26 financial results, **Rebel Foods' operating revenue increased 20 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,951.6 crore, while its losses declined 16.3 percent to Rs 281.8 crore.** The company has not yet reported its FY26 numbers, as stated in the source report.

**The Mumbai-based company has raised nearly $803 million in funding to date.** Its prominent investors include Peak XV Partners, Coatue, Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) and Lightbox.

Earlier this year, **Rebel Foods discontinued QuickiES, its 15-minute food delivery app, less than a year after its launch.** The decision followed high cash burn associated with the service.

Alongside Faasos, Behrouz Biryani and Oven Story Pizza, the company operates several other food brands, including Sweet Truth and The Good Bowl.

Kerten Hospitality Opens Cloud 7 Hotel The Forest Shimla

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Kerten Hospitality Opens Cloud 7 Hotel The Forest Shimla](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/jednfefnej.jpg)

Kerten Hospitality has announced the opening of Cloud 7 Hotel The Forest Shimla, expanding its presence in India’s hospitality market. The launch is part of the group’s plan to develop 1,000 keys across its Cloud 7, hosme and The House Hotel brands in India during its current expansion phase. ***Located amid the forests and hills of Shimla, the property combines accommodation, dining, wellness and leisure facilities.***

The hotel has opened with rooms and suites offering views of the Himalayas, while additional facilities are planned as part of a phased expansion. ***The planned additions include dedicated wellness suites, a destination spa, a swimming pool, a gym, two private cottages and nine additional luxury suites.*** These developments are intended to expand the property’s accommodation capacity and wellness offering over time.

> Marloes Knippenberg, CEO of Kerten Hospitality said, “***Cloud 7 Hotel The Forest Shimla reflects the strong momentum behind our growth journey in  India. The country offers significant potential for experience-led, lifestyle hospitality, and we are committed to building a meaningful long-term presence by working closely with owners and partners who share our vision. With an initial target of 1,000 keys, Shimla is an important step in creating a diverse portfolio of destinations that connect guests with local communities, culture and place.***”

The hotel incorporates elements of Himachal Pradesh’s culture and natural surroundings into its design and guest experiences. Its offering brings together accommodation, food and beverage, wellness activities, events and cultural programming, with an emphasis on local craftsmanship and engagement with regional communities.

A key feature of the property is The Observatory Bar, a rooftop lounge designed around views of the Himalayan landscape. The venue offers cocktails and whisky, with interiors featuring low lounge seating, handcrafted walnut furniture and copper detailing. ***A nautical telescope at the centre of the space allows guests to observe distant mountain peaks during the day and the moon and constellations after sunset.***

The bar’s beverage menu incorporates Himalayan botanicals and locally sourced ingredients. The hotel also offers outdoor terraces, event and meeting facilities, wellness activities and seasonal programmes, alongside art and cultural experiences linked to the region. ***The food and beverage programme has been curated by Michelin-starred chef Jaume Puigdengolas.*** It focuses on regional produce sourced from local farmers and suppliers, with sharing plates and seasonal menus that reinterpret mountain cuisine.

The property has also introduced Cloudfall Sessions, a daily sunset programme featuring curated music, a signature cocktail, a selected whisky, premium canapés and a dedicated service sequence. The initiative is intended to bring hotel guests and local residents together around the sunset views.

Cloud 7 Hotel The Forest Shimla plans to collaborate with artists and craftspeople from Shimla and other parts of Himachal Pradesh to showcase commissioned artwork, local photography, handmade ceramics and other craft products. Rotating exhibitions and cultural activities are also planned as part of the hotel’s programming. The property will work with regional farmers, suppliers of Himalayan ingredients, cultural organisations and tourism partners. ***These partnerships are intended to increase the participation of local businesses and creative communities in the hotel’s operations and guest experiences.***

Kerten Hospitality has identified India as a strategic market for its expansion. Through its Cloud 7, hosme and The House Hotel brands, the group plans to develop hospitality properties that combine accommodation with locally influenced dining, wellness and cultural experiences. The opening in Shimla marks another step in its stated target of reaching 1,000 keys across the country.

Ballard Pier Opens in Mumbai With Retail and Dining

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Ballard Pier Opens in Mumbai With Retail and Dining](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/yjtggttiuh.jpg)

The Ballard Pier Downtown Experience Centre has opened on Mumbai’s eastern waterfront, bringing together the Mumbai International Cruise Terminal, retail stores, restaurants and lifestyle spaces within a single development. ***The project, developed under the Mumbai Port Authority, aims to expand cruise tourism infrastructure in India while making the city’s historic harbour more accessible to residents and visitors.***

Located in the Ballard Estate precinct, the development houses the Mumbai International Cruise Terminal on its ground and first floors. The two upper levels, situated 17 and 21 metres above sea level, accommodate shopping, dining and entertainment facilities. ***The project combines passenger terminal operations with commercial spaces that can also serve visitors who are not travelling by cruise.***

The facility is operated by J M Baxi Ports and Logistics Private Limited under a 30-year concession agreement with the Mumbai Port Authority. Established in 1916, the J M Baxi Group has been involved in India’s shipping, ports and logistics sectors for 110 years. ***The Ballard Pier marks the group’s first consumer-facing maritime venture.***

***The opening comes as cruise operators expand their presence in India. Cordelia Cruises is introducing its second ship, Cordelia Sky, with a third vessel expected to follow.*** The development also comes amid growing interest from international cruise operators in the Indian market, supported by investments in passenger terminal infrastructure.

> Aditi Kotak, Director at Ballard Pier Private Limited said, “***We are privileged to be a part of shaping India’s cruising culture. Our coastline can become one of the country’s most distinctive tourism assets, but that takes more than infrastructure; it takes experiences that draw people to the sea. The Ballard Pier is our answer: a terminal that welcomes the world, and a destination that invites Mumbai to rediscover its waterfront.***”

The lifestyle and retail sections of The Ballard Pier are scheduled to open in phases over the next two months. ***The development will house a mix of Indian and international brands across fashion, beauty, accessories, home products, food and beverages.*** The dining and entertainment lineup includes Blue Frog, Titlie, Ministry of Crab, Voya Sea Club, Sorano, Naia, Naarma, TaiChi Café, Nandan Coffee, Yeti, 24k Kraft Brewzz, Olive Garden, Wolf of Grain, Flings Gelato Bar and Harbour House. These outlets will operate alongside cafés and other food and beverage establishments within the development.

The retail section will feature brands such as Nicobar, India Circus by Krsnaa Mehta, Le Chatelard 1802, Perona, Sweet Dreams, Lukson, Columbia, Daily Objects, Mokobara, Tuuli by Pooja, Vanilla Moon, Mija, Mulmul, Nykaa Luxe, Unrush and Aiza. The development will also include gourmet retail offerings from Rapsap and Urban Platter. ***The retail mix brings together fashion, beauty, travel accessories, lifestyle products and homegrown design brands, adding another shopping destination to Mumbai’s commercial retail market.*** The combination of retail and food and beverage outlets is intended to attract both cruise passengers and local consumers.

The Ballard Pier also includes a seaside seating area overlooking Mumbai’s eastern harbour. Located within the Ballard Estate heritage precinct, the space provides views of cruise ships, cargo vessels and other maritime activity. The development features a sea-facing glass facade and a combination of indoor and outdoor areas.

> Rahul Mehta of RM Architects, which worked on the project said, “***Our vision was to create a waterfront destination that belongs unmistakably to Mumbai, with the sea as its protagonist and architecture as its frame. By reimagining an existing port structure, we have opened it up to the city as a place to gather, discover and linger. Architecture comes alive not when a building is completed, but when people inhabit it and make it their own.***”

The terminal also incorporates environmental management measures. According to the operator, it is designed as a zero liquid discharge (ZLD) facility and will source 50 percent of its energy from solar power through a third-party partnership. The development includes in-house composting and used-oil collection systems that food and beverage operators can use for waste management. ***The Ballard Pier currently has a workforce comprising 50 percent women, with the operator targeting 70 percent female representation.***

The opening adds a combined cruise tourism, hospitality and retail development to Mumbai’s eastern waterfront. As additional retail and dining outlets become operational over the coming two months, The Ballard Pier is expected to serve both cruise passengers and Mumbai residents, while supporting the Mumbai Port Authority’s plans to develop the city as a cruise tourism hub.

London-founded tea brand Newby Teas has expanded its presence in New Delhi through new associations with Silver Lounge at The Lodhi and Café E at DLF Emporio. ***The additions extend the brand’s presence to three hospitality and lifestyle destinations in the capital, alongside its existing association with Café C at The Chanakya.***

![Crazy Cock Madhuca I Debuts at Bengaluru Duty Free](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/sjsncsnsj.jpg)

Crazy Cock Indian Single Malt Whisky and Six Brothers Mahura are being showcased at Bengaluru Duty Free, highlighting the use of mahua, an indigenous Indian flower, in the country's premium spirits market. ***The showcase brings together two products that use mahua in different ways, reflecting its place in traditional Indian culture and its growing use in contemporary spirits production.***

Crazy Cock Madhuca I is produced by South Seas Distilleries. ***The single malt whisky is matured in ex-brandy and ex-bourbon casks before being finished in ex-Mahura casks.*** Its flavour profile combines floral and earthy notes with fruit, spice and oak.

The expression received a Gold Medal at the World Whisky Masters 2026 and secured a top-three ranking at the International Wine & Spirit Competition (IWSC) UK 2026. The Bengaluru Duty Free showcase also features Six Brothers Mahura, a spirit made from mahua flowers and double-distilled in copper pot stills.

The product draws on the traditional use of mahua in India while presenting the ingredient in a contemporary spirits format. Its presence alongside Crazy Cock Madhuca I highlights two approaches to incorporating the indigenous flower into alcoholic beverages. ***Mahua has longstanding cultural and traditional associations in several parts of India.*** Its use in products such as Crazy Cock Madhuca I and Six Brothers Mahura reflects growing interest in incorporating indigenous ingredients into premium spirits.

***The showcase at Bengaluru Duty Free gives international travellers access to the two products and brings attention to mahua-based spirits within India's evolving beverage market.*** Travellers can find Crazy Cock Indian Single Malt Whisky Madhuca I and Six Brothers Mahura at Bengaluru Duty Free.

MITTI Café Adds New Inclusive Dining Outlet in Mumbai

![MITTI Café Adds New Inclusive Dining Outlet in Mumbai](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/sskwemmnb.jpg)

MITTI Café has opened an outlet at Sky City Mall in Borivali East, Mumbai, adding an inclusive food and beverage offering to the shopping destination. The café, located on the mall's lower ground level, is operated by persons with physical, intellectual, and psychiatric disabilities. ***The opening brings MITTI Café's employment-led hospitality model to Mumbai's western suburbs, giving mall visitors another option for coffee, beverages and meals while shopping or visiting the cinema.***

***MITTI Café began with a small table and an umbrella in Hubballi and has since expanded its operations to several prominent locations across India.*** Its outlets include Rashtrapati Bhavan, the Supreme Court of India, and major airports. The organisation has served more than 22 million meals and beverages through its network.

![JK Urbanscapes Invests Rs 110 Cr in Darjeeling Retreat](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/ssjnjnfrhjnbde.jpg)

JK Urbanscapes Developers Limited (JKUDL), part of JK Organisation, has partnered with Thailand-based Minor Hotels to develop Anantara Retreat Darjeeling Hills, a 70-key luxury hospitality project at Tindharia Tea Estate in West Bengal. ***The project involves an investment of Rs 110 crore by JK Urbanscapes in partnership with Kaushal Kumbhat and is scheduled to open in 2031.***

The development will mark the India debut of Anantara Retreats, a luxury hospitality concept under Anantara Hotels and Resorts. ***The project will combine accommodation, wellness services and tea-related experiences at a working plantation in the Eastern Himalayas.*** Located in Tindharia, approximately 40 km from Darjeeling town, the 849-acre tea estate sits at elevations ranging from 450 to 1,000 metres above sea level. The proposed retreat will be designed around the estate's existing landscape while tea cultivation continues.

> Abhishek Singhania, Chairman and Managing Director of JK Urbanscapes Developers Limited said, “***At JK Urbanscapes, we believe that exceptional developments begin with recognising the inherent potential of a place and preserving what makes it distinctive. Tindharia Tea Estate offers a rare opportunity to create a luxury hospitality destination that draws from the character of its landscape and the legacy of its tea-growing heritage. Our partnership with Minor Hotels brings together this distinctive setting and a globally renowned hospitality brand, reflecting our vision of building a portfolio of thoughtfully conceived destinations that offer enduring value while remaining deeply connected to their surroundings.***”

The proposed retreat will comprise 35 suites and 35 tented villas positioned along the tea estate's slopes. Planned facilities include an Anantara Spa, a fitness centre and a swimming pool overlooking the plantation and surrounding valley.

The wellness offering will include programmes informed by the region's natural environment and tea-growing heritage. A tea factory and tea garden will also be incorporated into the guest experience, allowing visitors to learn about tea cultivation and production. ***The project will additionally include 750 sq m of meeting and event space for meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE), as well as destination weddings.***

> Maneesh Mansingka, Joint Managing Director of JK Urbanscapes Developers Limited said, “***The development of Anantara Retreat Darjeeling Hills calls for an approach that is as thoughtful as it is commercially sound. The vision is to create a distinctive hospitality destination that draws from the natural character of Tindharia Tea Estate and its rich tea-growing heritage, while complementing the landscape in which it is set. By integrating accommodation, wellness and immersive tea-led experiences, we aim to create a retreat that offers guests a deeper connection with the destination while establishing a sustainable, long-term hospitality asset.***”

Anantara Retreats is a luxury hospitality concept under Anantara Hotels and Resorts, which is part of Minor Hotels. The concept focuses on secluded destinations and combines accommodation and personalised services with wellness programmes covering spa treatments, yoga, fitness, nutrition and mindfulness. ***The Darjeeling project will extend the group's presence in India through a retreat centred on the region's tea-growing heritage and natural surroundings.***

> Dillip Rajakarier, Group CEO of Minor International, the parent company of Minor Hotels said, “***Anantara Retreats belong in places that shape the stay, and Darjeeling does exactly that. Guests will settle into a working tea estate above the valley, follow the leaf from garden to factory and return to a wellness programme built around the same unhurried pace. We look forward to welcoming guests to Anantara Retreat Darjeeling Hills in 2031.***”

***Anantara Retreat Darjeeling Hills will be located approximately 33 km from Bagdogra International Airport, with road access expected to take around an hour.*** The airport connects the region with major Indian cities, including Delhi and Kolkata, as well as select international destinations.

The project adds to JK Urbanscapes' hospitality development portfolio and brings Minor Hotels' Anantara Retreats concept to a new market in India. With an opening planned for 2031, the development will add a luxury hospitality property to the Darjeeling region, with accommodation, wellness facilities and tea estate experiences forming its core offering.

These stores are more than new locations; they are another step towards making high-quality, approachable Korean food a regular part of everyday life for more people across India.***"

By combining CJ Foods' leading brand and product expertise with GTGO's deep local-market understanding and agile execution, we will bring the value of Korean food to more consumers across India.***"

Aspect Hospitality, the hospitality division of Aspect Global, has entered Mumbai’s premium dining segment with the launch of FITOUR, a new 14-seat restaurant in Bandra West. ***Opened on October 4, 2026, the concept focuses on Indian cuisine through a curated tasting menu format that combines food, design, storytelling, and sensory experiences.***

***The restaurant operates with a single seating and limited capacity, reflecting the growing demand for intimate and experience-led dining formats in India's hospitality sector.*** FITOUR’s menu is structured as a multi-course journey, with each course drawing inspiration from Indian ingredients, regional flavours, culinary traditions, and personal experiences. The dishes reinterpret familiar elements of Indian cuisine through contemporary techniques while maintaining a connection to their origins.

Beyond the menu, the dining experience incorporates sound, lighting, fragrance, textures, and curated beverage pairings to create a cohesive narrative for guests. Diners can choose from cocktail pairings, international wine pairings, or Indian wine pairings alongside the tasting menu. ***The restaurant’s interiors have been designed to complement the culinary experience.*** The space features terracotta tiles, woven natural materials, textured finishes, and understated décor that aligns with the overall concept.

***A key feature of the restaurant is the Nostalgia Wall, which displays photographs, handwritten recipes, personal memories, and artwork connected to the inspiration behind the menu.*** Guests can also view pickles, ferments, and hand-blended spices that form part of the kitchen’s preparation process, offering insight into the ingredients and techniques used throughout the experience.

Hitesh Keswani, Managing Director and CEO, Aspect Hospitality said, “FITOUR represents our vision of creating hospitality experiences that go beyond the conventional dining format. The concept brings together food, storytelling, design and sensory elements to create a distinctive and intimate experience for guests. Chef Ashwin’s culinary perspective has been central to shaping FITOUR, and we are pleased to introduce a concept that reflects both his journey and Aspect Hospitality’s approach to creating experiences with a strong point of view.”

Chef Ashwin Singh said, “FITOUR is a reflection of my journey with Indian cuisine and the experiences that have shaped my approach to food. The menu draws from memories, places, ingredients and techniques that have stayed with me over the years, while presenting them through a contemporary lens. I wanted to create an experience that extends beyond the food itself, with every element—from the flavours and pairings to the sound, lighting and design—contributing to the overall narrative.”

The tasting menu is priced at Rs 8,245 plus taxes, while cocktail pairings are available at Rs 5,495, international wine pairings at Rs 6,495, and Indian wine pairings at Rs 5,145, all exclusive of taxes. The launch highlights the continued expansion of experiential dining and chef-led hospitality concepts in India, where consumers are increasingly seeking curated culinary experiences beyond traditional restaurant formats.

***Menu offerings include products such as the Mexi-Crunch Burger, Korean Veggie Crunch Burger, Loaded Fries, samosa, crispers, desserts, and sundaes.*** Through the café format, the company is highlighting the versatility of its frozen food range while expanding its engagement with consumers.

> Aditya Krishna, Managing Director at McCain Foods India said, “***McCain has always enabled consumers to enjoy restaurant-like snacks and food experiences at home, made with high-quality ingredients they can trust. The McCain Signature Café takes this promise beyond the home, bringing to life the breadth and versatility of our portfolio through a wide range of recipes, flavours and formats. It gives consumers an opportunity to experience familiar McCain favourites in new ways, while enabling us to delight both consumers and customers with consistently high-quality, restaurant-style food experiences.***”

***Situated in one of Noida’s key retail and entertainment destinations, the café represents a new growth avenue for McCain in India’s foodservice and quick-service restaurant market.*** The company said the Signature Café is the first step in exploring a broader consumer-facing expansion strategy across selected locations. The launch reflects growing interest among food brands in creating direct-to-consumer experiences while strengthening brand visibility through experiential retail and foodservice formats.

![Retail India News: Alcobrew Expands with Gamber Valley Whisky Range](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/jbfrbefhue.jpg)

Alcobrew Distilleries India Limited has expanded its presence in the premium alcoholic beverages segment with the launch of Gamber Valley Indian Single Malt Whisky, marking its entry into the luxury whisky market in India. ***The new whisky range is distilled, matured, and bottled at the company's manufacturing facility in Solan, Himachal Pradesh.*** The portfolio includes Gamber Valley Private Collection 1, priced between Rs 13,000 and Rs 16,000, and Gamber Valley The Vault Series, priced between Rs 7,000 and Rs 10,000.

***The products will initially be available in Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Chandigarh, with plans to expand distribution to Rajasthan, Odisha, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Delhi NCT.***

> Romesh Pandita, Chairman and Managing Director, Alcobrew Distilleries India Limited said, "***Every generation has a window to build something that outlasts it. In spirits, that window is defined by the authenticity and purity in liquid you produce, the geography you choose to root yourself in, and the patience you bring to both. With Gamber Valley Indian Single Malt Whisky, we are not launching a product- we are building a legacy. We are of the belief that the world's most discerning whisky drinkers will, in time, reach for an Indian bottle with the same instinct they once reserved for other geographies. The data has been unambiguous for several years: a category growing rapidly annually, a consumer shifting decisively upward, and global recognition accelerating faster than most anticipated. The consumer at this price point is conscious of the purity, process and transparency. Everything about Gamber Valley Indian Single Malt Whisky, the geography of its distillation, the integrity of its ingredients, the patience of its maturation, has been built to withstand exactly that scrutiny. We have not entered this segment to participate. We have entered it to endure.***"

According to the company, the Solan-based distillery operates an integrated production model where distillation, maturation, and bottling are carried out at a single location. ***The facility's Himalayan climate forms part of the whisky-making process while allowing the company to oversee production at every stage.***

> Arvind Kaul, Deputy Managing Director, Alcobrew Distilleries India Limited said, "***Our Solan Unit was never just a distillery, it was a considered choice about geography, craft, and the long game. We chose the Himalayan heights of Solan because the altitude, humidity, and temperature cycles are not incidental to our process, they are the process. With complete control over distillation, maturation and bottling under one roof, we have the infrastructure to deliver consistency at scale without compromising on quality. What we are releasing today is only the first chapter of what this distillery is capable of.***"

The launch comes as India's premium whisky market, single malt whisky segment, and premium spirits industry continue to record growth. ***According to company data, India's whisky market was valued at Rs 1,610 billion in FY2024, accounting for approximately 70 percent of the country's total Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) market by value.*** The Indian single malt whisky market is expected to reach Rs 130 billion by FY2030, up from an estimated Rs 52 billion in FY2025, reflecting a CAGR of around 20 percent. In 2024, Indian single malts accounted for approximately 53 percent of total single malt case sales, surpassing imported Scotch whisky in volume terms for the first time.

Industry trends suggest demand is being supported by younger consumers, increasing disposable incomes, and growing interest in premium alcoholic beverages across both metro and non-metro markets.

> Ashutosh Rajput, Chief Operating Officer, Alcobrew Distilleries India Limited said, "***Indian single malts crossed 53 percent of total single malt volume in 2024 — that shift didn't happen by accident, and it isn't slowing down. The consumer driving this market is younger, better-travelled, and far less deferential to legacy labels than the generation before them. We are entering at a moment when the category is still being defined, which means the brands that build credibility now will own the narrative for the next decade. Our phased rollout is deliberate — we are building depth in each market before we move to the next, because this is a brand built to last, not to spike.***"

The launch reflects the broader premiumisation trend within India's alcoholic beverages sector, where spirits manufacturers are expanding their presence in the fast-growing single malt whisky category through new product offerings and region-specific production capabilities.

![Rola Opens New All-Day Diner in Bandra](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/ksknjdebnbdc.jpg)

Mumbai’s dining scene has welcomed a new addition with the launch of Rola, an all-day diner in Pali Hill, Bandra. Opened on 17 August 2026, the restaurant brings together breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner, specialty coffee, Neapolitan pizzas and Indian comfort food under one roof. ***With a seating capacity of 70 guests across indoor and outdoor spaces, Rola is positioned as a neighbourhood dining destination catering to a range of occasions, from morning coffee meetings and family meals to evening gatherings and casual dining.***

The restaurant's name is inspired by the energy and conversations often associated with shared dining experiences. ***An outdoor coffee cart welcomes guests at the entrance, complementing the brand's focus on coffee culture and all-day dining.***

> Puneet Anand, Founder, Rola said, "***For me, hospitality has always been about people. Good food is important, but it's the conversations, the warmth and the feeling of wanting to stay a little longer that people remember. That's the experience we wanted to create with Rola.***"

The menu spans multiple cuisines and meal occasions. ***Breakfast and brunch offerings include dishes such as Bombay Keema and Brun, featuring spiced mutton keema, fried egg and pav, and Benedict Goes Bandra, prepared with brioche, grilled chicken salami, hollandaise sauce and tandoori pineapple salsa.***

The restaurant also focuses on Indian comfort food through its House Kitchen section. ***Signature dishes include Khansama's Nihari, a slow-cooked nalli nihari, and Maa's Sunday Mutton Masala, served with buttered pav.***

Expanding its food offerings, Rola has introduced a range of Neapolitan pizzas, including the Kejriwal Pizza topped with egg, green chillies and cheese, and the Truffle Malai Chicken Tikka Pizza, which combines Indian flavours with traditional pizza-making techniques. ***Dessert options include Chai and Parle-G Cheesecake and Basque Cheesecake with raspberry compote, reflecting a mix of Indian-inspired and international dessert formats.***

Coffee remains a key part of the concept, supported by a dedicated beverage programme. Guests can choose from espresso-based drinks such as Flat White and Hot Spanish Latte, along with specialty beverages including Mint Charcoal Mocha, Sea Salt Vanilla Mocha, Coffee Tonic, and Affogato.

***Located in Pali Hill, Bandra, Rola aims to serve consumers seeking casual dining, specialty coffee, and all-day restaurant experiences.*** The average cost for two is approximately Rs 2,000. The opening reflects the continued growth of Mumbai's premium casual dining and café market, where operators are increasingly combining diverse food formats, coffee programmes and flexible dining experiences to attract urban consumers.

Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited has expanded its hospitality portfolio with the launch of Sterling Regalia Agra, a new hotel located near the Taj Mahal. ***The opening strengthens the company's presence in one of India's most visited tourism destinations and enhances its footprint across the Delhi-Agra-Jaipur Golden Triangle travel circuit.***

***Situated approximately 1.4 km from the Taj Mahal, the property offers access to Agra's key tourist attractions, local markets, heritage sites, and culinary experiences.*** The launch aligns with Sterling's broader strategy of expanding its hospitality network across major leisure and business travel destinations in India.

> Vikram Lalvani, Managing Director and CEO, Sterling Holiday Resorts said, "***Agra does not have a demand problem; it has a depth opportunity. The Taj brings the world to Agra. The opportunity for hospitality is to give travellers compelling reasons to stay longer, explore deeper and experience the city beyond its defining icon. Our Destination Architect strategy recognises that every destination needs a different intervention. In emerging destinations, we help create discovery; in established destinations like Agra, we build deeper engaging moments that connect them into larger travel circuits. Sterling Regalia Agra strengthens an important node in the Golden Triangle while opening up more of Agra to the bleisure traveller. The landmark creates the visit. The destination must create the journey.***"

The newly opened hotel features 36 rooms, a multi-cuisine restaurant, event facilities, and leisure amenities designed to cater to leisure travellers, families, corporate guests, and small groups. ***Among the property's key features is a rooftop swimming pool offering views of the Taj Mahal. The hotel also includes a top-floor deck for private gatherings and events.***

Its in-house restaurant, Regalia Spices, serves dishes inspired by Awadhi, Mughlai, and Braj cuisines, along with international menu options. The 40-seat dining space offers both buffet and à la carte services. ***Sterling said the property is positioned to support travellers looking to explore Agra beyond its iconic monument, including the city's Mughal heritage, local markets, food culture, and traditional crafts.***

> Capt. Brijesh Yadav and Dr. Rekha Yadav, Owners of Taj Regalia said, "***Our vision was to create an address that does justice to its location—close to one of the world’s most celebrated monuments, yet with a character and experience of its own. Sterling brings strong hospitality expertise, reach and a destination-led approach. Together, we want guests to remember Sterling Regalia Agra not simply for its proximity to the Taj Mahal, but for how they experienced Agra while staying with us.***"

***The company stated that the Agra property strengthens its participation in one of India's busiest tourism corridors.*** Located on the Golden Triangle route connecting Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur, the hotel is expected to cater to domestic and international tourists, family travellers, couples, group travellers, and business visitors. The opening is part of Sterling's ongoing destination-focused expansion strategy aimed at increasing its presence across key travel and hospitality markets in India.

![The Blondie House Opens New Community Café in Versova](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/ejebdende.jpg)

Bastian Hospitality has launched The Blondie House in Versova, bringing together its café brand Blondie and food concept Janu under one roof. The new multi-level hospitality destination combines an all-day café, bakery, Matcha Omakase experience, and a community-focused space designed for work, reading, social gatherings, and cultural events. ***Located in Mumbai’s Versova neighbourhood, The Blondie House expands on the concepts introduced at Blondie’s Bandra outlet and Janu, creating a new format that blends food, beverages, community engagement, and retail offerings.***

***The venue transitions from an all-day café and bakery on one level to a dedicated Matcha Omakase experience and shared community spaces.*** Features include a communal table, a curated library, a photobooth, in-house merchandise, and areas designed for guests to work, meet, and spend time. The space will also host workshops, tastings, readings, and small-format events.

The menu combines popular offerings from Blondie and Janu along with exclusive dishes created for The Blondie House. Breakfast selections include Eggs Japo Style with Miso Butter and the OG Blondie Avo Toast. Other menu highlights include Pretzel with Miso Honey Butter, Yaki Udon, Pani Puri, Raj Kachori, and Truffle Cheese Dosa. ***A frozen yogurt cart has also been introduced as part of the offering.***

***The bakery section features products such as the Pecan Miso Croissant Crown, Matcha Strawberry Tiffin, Sesame Tart, and Pineapple and Pandan Religieuse, alongside Blondie’s cookies and freshly baked viennoiserie.*** The House will also rotate seasonal bakes, homemade Greek yogurt, frozen yogurt, and gelato offerings.

Beverages remain a key focus, with a menu that includes speciality coffee, matcha-based drinks, filter coffee, milkshakes, mocktails, and signature beverages such as Mont Blanc, Yuzu Daydream, and Sakura. The dedicated Matcha Omakase concept expands on Blondie’s earlier matcha-focused experiences, exploring matcha preparation techniques, flavour pairings, and serving rituals.

***The interiors draw inspiration from Japanese hospitality and Scandinavian design, featuring concrete, wood, marble, handmade ceramics, natural materials, and greenery.*** The design also incorporates Blondie’s signature branding, including a custom-made La Marzocco Strada coffee machine created exclusively for the venue.

The hospitality concept also highlights products developed with women-led businesses, including handmade ceramics, house coffee blends sourced through women farmers, and a retail range featuring matcha, granola, and coffee products. A curated library focused on Korean and Japanese authors will support future community initiatives, including a planned book club.

> Ranjit Bindra, Founder, Bastian Hospitality said, “***The Blondie House is an evolution of how we think about hospitality, creating spaces that are not defined by a single meal or occasion, but become part of people’s everyday lives. Bringing Blondie and Janu together allows us to bring two distinct points of view to the same table: Blondie’s focus on coffee, matcha, and community, and Janu’s bold, playful take on Indian food. With The Blondie House, we wanted to create a destination that feels relevant from morning to evening, where people can come to eat, discover, work, connect and simply spend time. It is our way of reimagining what a neighbourhood hospitality space can be.***”

> Natasha Hemani, Brand Director, Blondie added, “***Blondie has always been about the details that make people want to come back, what they eat, what they drink, but also how they spend their time there. With The Blondie House, I wanted to take that feeling further. You can come in for a matcha, stay to work, pick up a book, take a photobooth strip or simply sit around with nowhere else to be. The House should feel beautiful, but also immediately yours.***”

Wyndham Hotels & Resorts has introduced Dolce Nova, a new upper-upscale hospitality brand positioned as an extension of Dolce Hotels & Resorts by Wyndham. **Inspired by the Italian concept of** ***il dolce far niente*****—translated as “the sweetness of doing nothing”—the new brand aims to cater to travellers seeking slower, more immersive and experience-driven stays.**

The launch marks Wyndham’s entry into the growing upper-upscale lifestyle hospitality segment, where demand is increasingly being driven by guests looking for authentic experiences, wellness-focused travel, and deeper connections with local culture.

**Dolce Nova has been designed around the principles of authenticity, discovery and a strong sense of place.** The brand seeks to encourage guests to slow down, engage more meaningfully with their surroundings and prioritize personal wellbeing during their travels.

**Building on the legacy of Dolce Hotels & Resorts, which has traditionally focused on meetings, events and resort experiences, Dolce Nova introduces a different hospitality proposition centered on connection, leisure and experiential travel.** The brand aims to create environments where guests can immerse themselves in local destinations while enjoying a more relaxed and intentional travel experience.

**Wyndham said the new offering responds to changing consumer preferences in the luxury and upper-upscale travel market.** Affluent travellers are increasingly prioritizing meaningful experiences, wellness and cultural engagement over traditional luxury markers, creating opportunities for hospitality brands to develop more personalized and purpose-driven experiences.

**The company noted that today's travellers are placing greater emphasis on authenticity, local immersion and thoughtful leisure experiences.** Dolce Nova has been developed to address these evolving expectations while providing hotel owners and developers with a differentiated brand proposition supported by Wyndham’s global distribution network and loyalty ecosystem.

**The launch also comes amid continued growth in the lifestyle hospitality sector.** Industry projections indicate that the global lifestyle hotel market is expected to witness significant expansion over the coming decade, driven by rising consumer demand for experiential travel and destination-led hospitality concepts.

**With Dolce Nova, Wyndham is expanding its portfolio to capture opportunities in the upper-upscale lifestyle segment while strengthening its presence among travellers seeking experience-led stays.** The company believes the new brand will appeal to both leisure travellers looking for meaningful connections and hotel owners seeking to capitalize on the growing demand for lifestyle-focused hospitality offerings.

**The introduction of Dolce Nova further reinforces Wyndham’s strategy of broadening its global hospitality portfolio with brands tailored to evolving travel preferences and emerging market opportunities.**

Curefoods Reports Rs 916 Cr Revenue in FY26 Amid Higher Net Losses

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Curefoods Reports Rs 916 Cr Revenue in FY26 Amid Higher Net Losses](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-19T113337.067.jpg)

Cloud kitchen and food services company Curefoods reported a 23 percent increase in operating revenue for FY26, reaching Rs 916.2 crore compared to Rs 745.8 crore in FY25. Despite the strong topline growth, **the company's net loss expanded to Rs 192.2 crore from Rs 170 crore a year earlier, reflecting continued pressure from depreciation and finance-related expenses.**

**Founded by Ankit Nagori, Curefoods operates a diversified portfolio of food brands spanning healthy meals, biryani, pizza, desserts, and South Indian cuisine.** Its brands include EatFit, Sharief Bhai Biryani, OLIO, Arambam, Krispy Kreme, Nomad Pizza, CakeZone, and Frozen Bottle. **The company currently serves customers through a network of 281 cloud kitchens, 99 kiosks, and 122 restaurants.**

**Revenue from food and product sales remained the primary contributor, accounting for nearly 99 percent of operating income.** This segment generated Rs 908.4 crore during FY26, marking a 23 percent increase year-on-year. The remaining Rs 7.8 crore came from services and other operating activities, including franchise-related fees.

**India continued to be the company’s largest market, contributing Rs 893.3 crore in revenue.** Meanwhile, international operations recorded significant growth, with overseas revenue increasing fourfold to Rs 22.85 crore.

**In addition to its core business income, Curefoods generated Rs 18.6 crore through non-operating sources such as interest income and gains from mutual fund investments.** This pushed its total income for the fiscal year to Rs 934.8 crore.

**Commission expenses climbed 22 percent to Rs 166.8 crore, while depreciation and amortisation charges rose 24 percent to Rs 100.6 crore.** In contrast, advertising and promotional spending declined 10 percent to Rs 79 crore during the year.

Other operating expenses, including rent, electricity, and professional services, amounted to Rs 256.3 crore. **As a result, total expenditure increased 19 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,127 crore.**

**Although losses widened, the company reported an improvement in operating efficiency.** Curefoods reduced its EBITDA loss to approximately Rs 69.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 86 crore in the previous year. Its EBITDA margin improved to negative 7.6 percent compared to negative 11.5 percent in FY25, indicating better cost management as revenue scaled.

**The company also improved its cost-to-revenue ratio, spending Rs 1.23 to generate every rupee of operating revenue, compared with Rs 1.27 in the previous fiscal year.**

However, liquidity indicators weakened during the year. Cash and bank balances declined 51 percent to Rs 39.4 crore at the end of FY26, while current assets fell 21 percent to Rs 267.7 crore.

**Curefoods had earlier secured approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed Rs 800 crore initial public offering after filing draft papers in October 2025.** The company subsequently paused its IPO plans due to volatile market conditions.

***The refreshed dining concept introduces 12 new vegetarian signature dishes along with a dedicated chaat menu inspired by Indore's well-known street food culture.*** The restaurant has also expanded its offerings by adding Chinese and Continental dishes to complement its existing Indian menu. The move marks a strategic shift for Tanatan, which will now operate exclusively as a vegetarian restaurant in a market where vegetarian dining continues to hold strong consumer appeal.

> Saurab Gahoi, Senior Vice President, Ramee Group of Hotels said, “***Tanatan has always been about creating memorable dining experiences. The dessert selection has also been expanded with Gulab Tres Leches, a preparation that combines gulkand, rose, saffron, and a three-milk base.

> Chef Roshan Seth said, “***We looked closely at what Indore already loves to eat and built the new menu around that. Nothing here is meant to be complicated. Every dish is 100 percent vegetarian and has a reason behind it, whether it comes from an old family recipe or a street food memory. We wanted guests to taste something familiar, even in the dishes that are entirely new to the menu.***”

![{Funding Alert} The Pizza Bakery Parent Popo Global Secures Rs 532 Cr Funding for National Expansion](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-11T113833.224.jpg)

Bengaluru-based restaurant operator Popo Global, the company behind popular food brands The Pizza Bakery, Paris Panini and Smash Guys, has raised Rs 532 crore (approximately $56 million) in funding from investment firm Artal Asia.

**The fresh investment will be used to strengthen the company’s presence across India by opening new outlets and expanding its portfolio of food and beverage brands.**

**Popo Global follows a company-owned and operated model rather than relying on franchise partnerships.** This approach enables the business to maintain direct oversight of operations, customer experience, and quality standards across all its locations.

**Founded by brothers Abhijit Gupta and Nikhil Gupta, the company launched The Pizza Bakery in Bengaluru in 2017.** Since then, it has grown the brand significantly while diversifying its offerings through the addition of Paris Panini and Smash Guys.

**Over the years, Popo Global has built a network of company-run outlets catering to both the casual dining and quick service restaurant (QSR) segments, positioning itself as a growing player in India’s organized foodservice industry.**

Popo Global had been in discussions with global private equity firm Invus Group to raise nearly Rs 500 crore through a minority stake sale. **The deal was reportedly expected to value the company between Rs 1,100 crore and Rs 1,350 crore.**

**Popo Global generated approximately Rs 175 crore in revenue during FY25 and remained profitable during the fiscal year.** The latest funding round is expected to provide additional momentum for the company’s growth strategy as it scales its restaurant brands and expands into new markets across India.

Aditya Birla New Age Hospitality Launches Supa San in Bandra

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Aditya Birla New Age Hospitality Launches Supa San in Bandra](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/ksxkjdnbx.jpg)

Aditya Birla New Age Hospitality (ABNAH) has launched Supa San, a new Japanese izakaya-inspired restaurant in Bandra West, Mumbai. Located on the 14th floor of Mansionz One on Linking Road, the 110-seater outlet marks the brand’s latest expansion in the premium dining and hospitality segment. ***The concept combines Japanese cuisine, cocktails, music culture, and experiential dining under one roof.***

***Following the success of its BKC outlet, which drew inspiration from manga and anime culture, Supa San Bandra takes a different direction by focusing on Japan’s music culture.*** The restaurant incorporates elements of listening bars, vinyl cafés, neighbourhood eateries, record stores and karaoke culture into its overall experience.

The food menu features more than 100 dishes across categories such as small plates, sushi, tempura, robata grills, ramen and larger-format Japanese dishes. ***Nearly 50 percent of the menu is vegetarian, reflecting growing consumer demand for plant-based and vegetarian dining options in India's restaurant industry.*** Among the restaurant’s signature offerings are Kamameshi, a traditional Japanese rice preparation cooked in an iron pot, and Mazeman, a broth-free ramen dish. The menu also includes dishes such as Hamachi Tiradito, Otoro Tataki and Kinmedai, alongside a range of sushi and robata-grilled selections.

***The beverage programme, titled NOW PLAYING, has been designed around music themes and features cocktails inspired by Japanese artists, genres and soundtracks.*** The drinks menu is divided into five sections, allowing guests to choose beverages based on flavour profiles and intensity. The restaurant also offers a dedicated non-alcoholic drinks menu featuring Japanese teas, matcha, hojicha and cold brew options.

***Beyond food and beverages, Supa San includes interactive dining elements such as complimentary otōshi, tableside rituals and Omikuji fortune draws presented with the bill.*** The venue will also host resident DJs, guest performances and music-focused programming, with weekends geared towards a more energetic social experience.

> Udai Pinnali, CEO, Aditya Birla New Age Hospitality said, “***At ABNAH, we see hospitality as increasingly moving beyond food and service towards creating a deeper cultural connection. With Supa San Bandra, we have taken the Japanese izakaya as a starting point and explored it through one of Japan’s most influential cultural forces - music. The concept comes from a genuine appreciation of Japan - its literature, manga, music, design, and food - but the intention is not to replicate Japan. It is to interpret these cultural codes through a contemporary lens that feels relevant to Mumbai. Every element, from the culinary programme developed by chefs trained in Japanese cuisine to the music, design and programming, is designed to give guests a more considered understanding of the culture and the stories behind it. For us, Supa San is therefore not simply about serving Japanese food. It is about creating a place where food becomes an entry point into a broader cultural experience - one that can resonate with people who know and love Japan, as well as those discovering it for the first time. Bandra, with its openness to culture, creativity and new forms of socialising, felt like the natural setting for this interpretation of contemporary Japan.***”

***Designed by Patch Design Studio, the restaurant incorporates influences from Japanese urban culture through communal dining areas, private seating spaces and an open-air alfresco section.*** The venue also features The Sound Archive, developed in collaboration with Roland, showcasing synthesizers, drum machines and music equipment associated with various genres. Another feature, The Culture Shelf, combines collectibles, vinyl records, merchandise and memorabilia inspired by Japanese music culture.

The restaurant also houses a private karaoke room, which will host weekly community-led karaoke sessions and be available for private events and celebrations.

The launch reflects growing demand for experiential dining, themed restaurants, Japanese cuisine and premium hospitality concepts in Mumbai’s food and beverage sector, with operators increasingly combining entertainment, culture and food-led experiences to attract consumers.

Delhi-based burger chain Perilicious – Smash Burgers and Grills has expanded its footprint in the National Capital Region with the launch of a new 43-seater outlet in Greater Kailash 2 (GK 2), M Block. ***The new location introduces draught beer, wine and cocktail offerings alongside the brand’s existing range of smash burgers, grilled dishes and casual dining menu items.***

Founded by Raihan Bham, Krishnam Duggal, Devinder Verma, and Nikunj Gaba, Perilicious started operations in February 2024 with a 20-seater outlet in Malviya Nagar. The brand has since grown its presence in the quick service restaurant (QSR) and casual dining segment, with customer feedback playing a key role in shaping its menu and expansion plans.

***Over time, the company has increased its focus on smash burgers while continuing to offer grilled food as a core category.*** Its current menu includes grilled chicken, rice bowls, loaded fries, chicken tenders, desserts, sauces, smashed tacos, hot dogs and small plates. The Mushroom Melt remains one of the vegetarian options within its burger range. The newly opened GK 2 outlet marks an expansion of the brand’s format, with the addition of draught beer, wine and lighter cocktails. The beverage selection includes beer- and wine-based drinks such as Michelada, White Wine Picante and Red Wine Float.

> Nikunj Gaba, Co-Founder of Perilicious said, “***GK is where we finally got to have a little more fun with Perilicious - the burgers and grills people already know us for, now with cold beer, wine and a lot more energy around the table. It feels bigger, louder and much closer to the brand we always wanted to build.***”

Perilicious currently operates three outlets and a centralised kitchen. ***The brand's 40-seater outlet at Elan Epic Mall in Gurgaon marked its first expansion outside Delhi.*** With the launch of the GK 2 outlet, the company continues to strengthen its position in the growing burger restaurant and casual dining market.

The brand has outlined plans to reach 10 stores by the end of 2027, reflecting continued growth in the organised food service sector. The latest opening also signals a broader strategy to combine food and beverage experiences within its restaurant network as it scales operations across Delhi NCR.

![Dodicci Opens New European Dining Space in Delhi](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/eeknghmyhk.jpg)

Delhi’s hospitality and fine dining landscape has expanded with the launch of Dodicci, a new European dining destination at The Ashoka Hotel, Chanakyapuri. ***The restaurant introduces an Italian-led European menu that combines influences from across the continent while offering a contemporary dining and cocktail experience.***

Built around the concept of “***La Casa Europa***”, Dodicci is designed as a modern European home where food, beverages, music, and hospitality come together in a relaxed setting. Rather than focusing on a single cuisine, the restaurant brings together culinary influences from Italy, France, wider Europe, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia.

The name Dodicci, which translates to "twelve" in Italian, forms the foundation of the restaurant’s concept. ***The venue is imagined as a home inhabited by twelve residents, each represented through a collection of twelve signature cocktails, with every drink reflecting a distinct personality and story.***

The menu features a mix of European classics and contemporary interpretations. Guests can choose from hand-rolled pastas, pizzas, Poulet Rôti with potatoes, Spanish croquettes, Brazilian tapioca parmesan, and lemon meringue tart, among other offerings. ***The culinary approach focuses on high-quality ingredients and modern techniques while drawing inspiration from traditional European dishes.***

The kitchen is led by Chef Gurdev, whose culinary experience spans France and Italy. A graduate of Le Cordon Bleu, Paris, she has worked at the two-Michelin-starred Le Taillevent and alongside Chef Inaki Aizpitarte of Le Chateaubriand. Her professional journey also includes culinary assignments across Paris, Saint-Tropez, and Italy’s Veneto region.

In Delhi, Chef Gurdev is also known for and Daughters…, an invitation-only chef’s table experience that she has operated from her South Delhi residence for more than five years. Her cooking style, which combines European culinary training with an evolving and flexible approach to menu development, shapes the restaurant’s food philosophy.

The interiors of Dodicci have been designed to reflect the atmosphere of a contemporary European residence. ***The space incorporates earthy colours, minimal design elements, handwritten details, ambient lighting, and curated music to create an informal dining environment.***

Located within The Ashoka Hotel, the restaurant enters Delhi’s growing premium dining and hospitality market at a time when consumers are increasingly seeking international cuisine, curated dining experiences, and destination-led food concepts. With its focus on European cuisine, signature cocktails, and experiential dining, Dodicci adds a new offering to the capital’s restaurant landscape.

How Pour Over’s Sibling Duo Is Redefining India’s Coffee Experience

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![How Pour Over’s Sibling Duo Is Redefining India’s Coffee Experience](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-08/pour%20over.jpg)

Most family businesses in Indian hospitality begin with a recipe. This one began with an argument about grind size.

Ritika and Aditya Sharma, who run Pour Over Coffee Roasters, are among a small group of sibling founders reshaping how India drinks coffee. On Raksha Bandhan, a festival built around what a brother and sister owe each other, the two made the day in the least sentimental way available to them, at a cupping table in Khan Market, tasting through the last of the season's Colombian arrivals.

The division of labour is settled by now. Aditya, a certified coffee professional who spent four years on a diploma at the Espresso Academy in Florence, runs the coffee programme, the sourcing and the roast.

Ritika drives the business, the formats and the expansion. Between them they have taken a store in store roastery in Malviya Nagar and turned it into a brand operating out of Khan Market, the Santushti Complex in Chanakyapuri, Noida and, since June, McLeodganj.

**The Colombian season**

The most visible piece of that work this year has been the Colombian Collection, a limited run of lots from Huila that landed in July and is available across all four cafés.

Two have carried the season. The Papayo Natural comes in with pineapple, tropical fruit and berry, a silky body and a bright line of acidity. The Colombian Blend Natural is the rounder of the pair, layered with red fruit, cacao and a sweetness closer to wine. The Papayo was picked in January at Acevedo in Huila, fermented naturally for 96 hours and given a medium roast.

Each cup arrives with a card carrying the origin, the SCA cup score, the harvest, the process and the roast level. It is a small thing that has done more for the brand's reputation among serious drinkers than any campaign.

> "Every lot in this collection was selected because it represented something unique, a producer, a process, a variety or a story worth sharing," Ritika Sharma said. "This launch is not about importing coffee from another country. It is about building a bridge between origin and cup, between producer and consumer, and between Colombia and India."

**Indian beans, roasted in house**

The imports sit alongside what remains the base of the business. Pour Over works only with 100 per cent Arabica single origin beans from estates in Chikmagalur, Coorg and Sikkim, roasted in micro lots at its own roastery and held in climate controlled storage. International coffees from Ethiopia, Colombia, Mexico, Costa Rica and Indonesia round out the range.

Aditya Sharma has described the approach as stripping the process back rather than dressing it up. "From sourcing to cup, each stage is consciously driven, keeping global marketplace value in mind, its impact to livelihood and coffee innovation, yet removing the fluff and providing authentic, honest and seriously brewed coffee, accessible by everyone," he said.

The work that gets least attention is the fermentation. Direct relationships with producers have let the roastery push processing at origin rather than pick from what is already on offer, which is a slower way to build a coffee list and a harder one to explain.

**Cupping, in public**

Cupping is the trade's own tasting method, a fixed ritual of grind, steep, break and slurp that buyers use to score a lot before they commit to it. It is normally done behind a closed door. At Pour Over it is run in the café, in front of whoever has walked in that morning, and Aditya Sharma is the one at the table.

His training is what makes the session work. The Florence diploma was four years of exactly this, learning to place a coffee by taste alone, and he now walks customers through the same sequence he uses to decide what the roastery buys.

On the brewing that follows, he keeps the framing plain. "Our brewing culture is simple, come over to our café and enjoy your cup brewed to precision from temperature to ratio, or request for beans ground to your size and choice of house blends," he said.

For Ritika, the sessions are the argument for the whole business. "Once people can taste the difference for themselves in an open, unintimidating setting, quality stops being a luxury conversation and starts being an obvious choice," she said. "That's the slower, more deliberate kind of scale we're betting on."

She is direct about where the growth is. "The biggest untapped opportunity isn't in the metros anymore. It's in the Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities where a large, aspirational, digitally native consumer base is already primed but hasn't yet been offered better coffee in a way that's accessible rather than intimidating."

**After dark**

The Khan Market flagship, revamped this year, now runs from 7 am to midnight on an AM PM format that turns a coffee bar into a cocktail bar as the evening comes on.

The espresso martini is built with vodka, espresso, house made coffee liqueur and cacao buttermilk. Among the cold brews, the Golden Brew sets mango against the bitterness of the coffee, while the Red Eye Salsa runs tomato and jalapeño through it and divides opinion on purpose.

**What comes next**

Expansion runs on three tracks. More retail in key Indian markets, deeper business to business supply into hotels, restaurants and institutions, and Indian specialty coffee taken abroad through hospitality partnerships.

"Our focus is on building Pour Over into a strong, profitable and scalable Indian coffee brand, rather than pursuing growth at any cost," Ritika Sharma said. "Build a strong unit economics model at every location and channel, then use that foundation to scale the brand sustainably."

Whether the cupping table stays in the middle of it, on Raksha Bandhan or any other day, is one thing the two of them do not appear to disagree about.

![Contemporary Mexican Restaurant Selva Launches in Delhi](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-08/Everlite%20by%20Senco%20names%20Wamiqa%20Gabbi%20as%20its%20first%20national%20brand%20ambassador%20%2811%29.jpg)

Contemporary Mexican restaurant Selva has entered the Delhi market with the opening of its newest outlet at World St., Worldmark, Aerocity, adding another international-inspired dining concept to the capital’s growing food and beverage landscape.

**The restaurant marks the third hospitality venture by Sarthak Sidana, founder of Underdoggs and Sere, who has developed restaurant concepts across 10 Indian cities over the past decade.**

**Selva’s culinary offering is inspired by regional Mexican cuisine while incorporating elements of Japanese-Peruvian Nikkei gastronomy.** According to the company, the menu has been shaped by more than a year of research and exploration across Mexico and parts of Asia to better understand the traditions and techniques behind the cuisines.

**The menu features dishes such as Tlayuda, Nori Tacos, ceviches, tiraditos, house-made tortillas, and a selection of robata-grilled seafood and meats, bringing together flavours and cooking styles from multiple culinary traditions.**

**In addition to its dining experience, the venue includes Selva Maya, an evening cocktail bar influenced by themes from Mesoamerican mythology.** The beverage programme has been curated by the team behind Goa’s Hideaway Cocktail Bar, known for its craft cocktail offerings.

> **S. K. Sayal, Managing Director and CEO, Bharti Real Estate said**, “Selva’s arrival is a strong reflection of World St.‘s growing stature as India’s most sought-after culinary destination. We have always envisioned World St. as a space that brings the world’s most distinctive dining experiences to Delhi. As World St. continues to welcome celebrated brands, we remain committed to making this promenade a true benchmark for experiential dining in the country.”

> **Sarthak Sidana, Founder, Selva, shared,** “Selva is a culmination of our deep rooted love & years spent travelling, researching and understanding cuisines & cultures across Mexico, Peru, Japan and beyond. We wanted to challenge the way Mexican & Nikkei cuisine is understood in India. This wasn’t about recreating what we had experienced elsewhere, but about understanding the cuisine at its roots and finding our own expression of it, one where the food, cocktails, design and hospitality come together to create an experience that feels both rooted and unexpected.”

**The opening further strengthens the culinary portfolio of World St., a destination that has increasingly attracted global and premium food and beverage brands.** The promenade is already home to several well-known dining concepts, including Olive Garden’s first India outlet, PF Chang’s, Magnolia Bakery, Starbucks Reserve, and Paul. **Additionally, Time Out Market is expected to make its India debut at the location.**

Spread across Worldmark 4, 5, and 6, World St. spans nearly half a kilometre and has been designed as a pedestrian-friendly boulevard featuring restaurants, cafés, bars, landscaped courtyards, public spaces, and art installations.
